headline: Record quarter, guidance raised across every metric
summary_short: Total revenue rose 47.7% y/y (and 27.7% q/q) to $481.0M as record royalty revenue of $307.7M (+49.6% y/y) drove the quarter, while non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.28 (+48.1% y/y) beat the year-ago print and Halozyme raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, royalty revenue, adjusted EBITDA and EPS.
summary_long: Total revenue reached $481.0M (+47.7% y/y), driven mainly by 49.6% royalty-revenue growth from ENHANZE partner products (VYVGART Hytrulo, DARZALEX SC) plus a 59.0% jump in product sales. Operating expenses rose on higher cost of sales (bulk rHuPH20), R&D and SG&A, and acquisition-related intangible amortization (Elektrofi, Surf Bio), but revenue growth outpaced expense growth, so operating income still grew 42.1% y/y to $287.7M and net income rose 39.2% y/y to $229.9M. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.28 (+48.1% y/y). The company repurchased $332.8M of shares in the quarter. Cash plus marketable securities rose to $231.9M from $145.4M at 2025 year-end. Halozyme raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, royalty revenue, adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP EPS.

drivers.explanation: Release attributes the 48% y/y gain mainly to royalty revenue growth plus higher product sales; no further product-sales-specific driver is given.
Growth reflects continued sales uptake of ENHANZE partner products launched since 2020, predominantly VYVGART Hytrulo (argenx) and DARZALEX SC (Janssen), plus other recently launched products.
Y/y growth reflects the overall revenue commentary citing 'an increase in product sales'; the release gives no product-specific cause. Q/q was roughly flat, implying growth is concentrated y/y.
Revenue grew $155.3M y/y while total operating expenses grew $70.1M, so income expanded despite cost of sales, R&D, SG&A and amortization all rising on bulk rHuPH20 sales and 2025 acquisitions.
Follows operating income's growth (revenue outpacing expense growth), partly offset by income tax expense rising in line with higher pretax income.
Tracks net income's 39.2% y/y growth; a smaller diluted share count from ongoing buybacks lifted per-share growth slightly above net-income growth.
Non-GAAP EPS adds back share-based compensation, debt-discount and intangible amortization, and IP litigation costs to GAAP EPS, per the company's own reconciliation table.
Follows operating income's growth plus a depreciation/amortization add-back, adjusted to exclude $6.9M of Merck patent-litigation costs the company excludes as non-recurring.
Release states the increase was primarily driven by cash generated from operations.
Share count fell as the company repurchased 4.8 million shares for $332.8 million during the quarter under its buyback program.

CEO cited record revenue, royalty growth and adjusted EBITDA strength, plus five new ENHANZE/Hypercon collaborations signed YTD (Vertex, Oruka, GSK, Incyte, one undisclosed), as the basis for raising FY2026 guidance.
